paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence “College provides a great opportunity for students to explore various possibilities and find the right path for themselves.” You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：对于这一部分，你有 30 分钟的时间写一篇文章，开头是“大学为学生提供了一个很好的机会来探索各种可能性并找到适合自己的道路。”您可以发表评论、引用示例或利用您的个人经历来完善您的论文。你应该写至少150字但不超过200字。

paragraphs.sourceText: You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您应该复制论文开头引号中给出的句子。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，有一段有十个空格。您需要从文章后面的单词库中给出的选项列表中为每个空白选择一个单词。在做出选择之前仔细阅读该段落。银行中的每个选择都由一个字母标识。请在答题卡 2 上的每个项目上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。您不得多次使用银行中的任何单词。

paragraphs.sourceText: About 23% of the global population lives in absolute poverty. In developing countries there is a low life expectancy, a high infant 26 rate, high levels of unemployment and illiteracy, nutritional levels below acceptable standards and widespread disease with very little or poor quality medical assistance. Others live 27 wealthy and luxurious lives and so the wealth is distributed in a very 28 manner. These are the central problems to questions of charity though charity also includes many other areas such as assisting the elderly.
paragraphs.translationZh: 全球约 23% 的人口生活在绝对贫困之中。在发展中国家，预期寿命低，婴儿死亡率高，失业率和文盲率高，营养水平低于可接受的标准，疾病广泛传播，而医疗援助却很少或质量很差。其他人过着极其富裕和奢华的生活，因此财富的分配方式非常不平等。这些是慈善问题的核心问题，尽管慈善还包括许多其他领域，例如帮助老年人。

paragraphs.sourceText: We all 29 when very rich people pledge to give away most of their billions, but they are usually left with millions to pass on, still much more than most people would expect to earn in their lifetime. Even comparatively 30 salaries in the west are very high when compared globally. Someone on £20,000 could easily afford to give away £2,000 per year and still have plenty to live on plus some luxuries.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当非常富有的人承诺捐出大部分数十亿美元时，我们都会鼓掌，但他们通常会留下数百万美元可以传承，仍然远远超过大多数人一生的预期收入。与全球相比，即使是西方相对中等的工资也非常高。拥有 20,000 英镑的人可以轻松承担每年捐赠 2,000 英镑的费用，并且仍然有足够的生活费和一些奢侈品。

paragraphs.sourceText: Most people agree that giving to charity is morally 31 but charitable behaviour tends to be regarded as above and beyond the call of duty. Some argue, however, that charitable behaviour is morally required. This means that to fail to behave charitably would be wrong. The majority of arguments in this vein refer to giving aid to poorer nations but they may also refer to giving time within one’s 32 community. Arguments tend to place different requirements on people in different income brackets and 33 entirely people who are merely making ends meet. Some argue that people should all contribute a certain percentage of their earnings. I will 34 together all those arguments that place a moral requirement on people to give to charity, despite the fact that there is wide disagreement as to the 35 of that moral requirement.
paragraphs.translationZh: 大多数人都认为，慈善捐赠在道德上是值得赞扬的，但慈善行为往往被认为超出了职责范围。然而，有些人认为慈善行为是道德上所必需的。这意味着不表现慈善行为就是错误的。大多数这种观点都是指向较贫穷的国家提供援助，但也可能指在自己的直接社区中给予时间。争论往往对不同收入阶层的人提出不同的要求，并完全排除那些仅仅维持收支平衡的人。一些人认为，人们都应该贡献其收入的一定比例。我将把所有那些对人们捐赠慈善事业提出道德要求的论点放在一起，尽管事实上人们对于道德要求的程度存在广泛的分歧。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: The Free-Trade Paradox
paragraphs.translationZh: 自由贸易悖论

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Trade is one of the policy areas where the hostility that exists between populists (民粹主义者) and classical liberals is most visible. Free-traders point to the undeniable good that tariff-free trade has done for consumers across the world and to the observable alleviation of poverty in corners of the world where previously closed markets have been opened up. Protectionists point to the domestic producers who’ve paid the price for this globalized economy in the form of lost livelihoods and hollowed-out communities.
paragraphs.translationZh: A）贸易是民粹主义者与古典自由主义者之间敌对最为明显的政策领域之一。自由贸易者指出，免关税贸易为世界各地的消费者带来了不可否认的好处，并且在世界各个角落，以前封闭的市场被开放后，贫困现象明显减轻。保护主义者指出，国内生产商为全球化经济付出了失去生计和社区空心化的代价。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) The ongoing conservative civil war often degenerates into content-free tribal warfare, but trade is a rare exception. There are substantial, thought-out policy proposals on both sides of the argument.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 正在进行的保守派内战常常会退化为毫无内容的部落战争，但贸易是一个罕见的例外。争论双方都提出了实质性的、经过深思熟虑的政策建议。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Consequently, trade as a topic of discussion provides an opportunity for liberals and populists to have a real meeting of minds. Fruitful debates might actually take place in this area, as opposed to the familiar ritual we’ve become accustomed to of condemnation met with counter-condemnation.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 因此，贸易作为一个讨论话题为自由主义者和民粹主义者提供了真正达成共识的机会。富有成效的辩论实际上可能会在这一领域发生，而不是我们已经习惯的谴责与反谴责的熟悉仪式。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) Strange as it might sound, the problem with trade in the modern world isn’t a matter of dollars and cents. It’s a matter of false consciousness. This observation is bound to set Marxist alarm bells ringing in the minds of some readers, but it was first made by Alexis de Tocqueville in 1840.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 尽管听起来很奇怪，现代世界的贸易问题并不是美元和美分的问题。这是错误意识的问题。这一观察必然会给一些读者敲响马克思主义的警钟，但它是由亚历克西斯·德·托克维尔于 1840 年首次提出的。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) Tracking the economic development of mankind from primitive to modern societies, Tocqueville observed a paradox unfolding over the centuries as economic realities and human experience of those realities strayed further and further from each other. In primitive societies, he notes, the division of labor was as yet undeveloped for the most part, requiring each person, family, or tribe to be relatively independent when it came to meeting their own basic material needs. Men built their own dwellings, farmed their own land, tended to their own livestock. This is not to deny that basic forms of trade took place, but, for the most part, our primitive ancestors lived fairly self-reliant, if crushingly poor, lives.
paragraphs.translationZh: E）托克维尔追踪人类从原始社会到现代社会的经济发展，观察到几个世纪以来随着经济现实和人类对这些现实的经验越来越背离而出现的悖论。他指出，在原始社会，劳动分工在很大程度上尚未发展，要求每个人、家庭或部落在满足自己的基本物质需求时相对独立。人们建造自己的住宅，耕种自己的土地，饲养自己的牲畜。这并不是否认基本形式的贸易的存在，但在大多数情况下，我们的原始祖先过着相当自力更生的生活，尽管生活极其贫困。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) However, the exclusively local and face-to-face nature of economic and political organization in the ancient and prehistoric worlds constantly impressed upon these primitive peoples the uncontrollable reality of others and their needs. As Tocqueville notes, “as soon as a man begins to deal with common affairs in public, he begins to perceive that he is not so independent of his fellow men as he had first imagined, and that in order to obtain their support he must often lend them his cooperation.”
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 然而，古代和史前世界中经济和政治组织的独特的地方性和面对面的性质不断地给这些原始民族留下深刻的印象：他人及其需求是无法控制的现实。正如托克维尔所指出的，“一个人一旦开始在公共场合处理公共事务，他就开始意识到自己并不像他最初想象的那样独立于同胞，为了获得他们的支持，他必须经常与他们合作。”

paragraphs.sourceText: G) At the advent of the modern world, the division of labor spread further and further throughout society. Each person became more and more dependent on others for their basic needs. And yet, robbed of the engagement with our neighbors and with our local communities that our ancestors were forced into by circumstance, we feel ourselves to be more and more independent of one another. As we become more and more dependent on others, we become less and less conscious of our dependence on others. This is the paradox of trade in the modern world.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 随着现代世界的到来，劳动分工在整个社会中越来越广泛地蔓延。每个人的基本需求都变得越来越依赖他人。然而，由于我们的祖先因环境而被迫与邻居和当地社区进行接触，我们感到自己越来越独立。当我们越来越依赖他人时，我们就会越来越不意识到自己对他人的依赖。这就是现代世界贸易的悖论。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) The false consciousness that this paradox generates causes havoc on the debates we have about free trade. There is scarcely a single commodity in any American household that isn’t dependent for its manufacture and sale, through one supply chain or another, on scores of different people spread out across the entire globe. But as Tocqueville already foresaw in 1840, we do not feel dependent on these strangers for our way of life. No sense of the dependence of our own material welfare on their work ever strikes our national consciousness. We rarely contemplate the globalized avenues of free trade with gratitude.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 这种悖论产生的错误意识对我们关于自由贸易的辩论造成了严重破坏。在任何一个美国家庭中，几乎没有一种商品的制造和销售不依赖于分布在全球各地的数十个不同的人，通过一个供应链或另一个供应链。但正如托克维尔在 1840 年就预见到的那样，我们并不觉得自己的生活方式依赖于这些陌生人。我们的民族意识从未意识到我们自己的物质福利依赖于他们的工作。我们很少怀着感激之情思考自由贸易的全球化途径。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) There are two reasons for this. The first, to put it bluntly, is money. Money allows us to purchase the work of others without giving any thought to them as human beings. Unlike our ancestors in their primitive townships, we rarely have to meet face-to-face the people who’ve invented, built, shipped, or supplied our goods. No relationship has to be built before an exchange can take place. Simply agree on a price, and you can have any goods you wish without taking a second thought for the human being involved on the other side of the transaction. In this way, money makes us feel more independent than we actually are. Each of us senses the hold that it has over our fellows. We know that if we bid highly enough we can buy ourselves out of the time-consuming labor of building relationships. Money is kind of like magic in that way. It gives us a set of rituals to perform and promises that if we do so we’ll be able to wield power over others. The illusion is created that having enough money to buy something is the equivalent of knowing how to make it yourself. Gratitude for the anonymous men and women who make up the supply chain rarely makes its way into our consciousness.
paragraphs.translationZh: I）这有两个原因。第一个，说白了就是钱。金钱让我们能够购买他人的作品，而不用将他们视为人。与我们在原始城镇的祖先不同，我们很少需要面对面地见到发明、建造、运输或供应我们商品的人们。在进行交换之前无需建立任何关系。只需商定价格，您就可以拥有您想要的任何商品，而无需再考虑交易另一方的人员。这样，金钱让我们感觉比实际更独立。我们每个人都感觉到它对我们同胞的控制力。我们知道，如果我们出价足够高，我们就可以摆脱建立关系的耗时劳动。从这个角度来看，金钱有点像魔法。它为我们提供了一套要执行的仪式，并承诺如果我们这样做，我们将能够对他人行使权力。这就产生了一种错觉，认为有足够的钱买东西就相当于知道如何自己制作东西。我们很少意识到对构成供应链的匿名男女的感激之情。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Anonymity, in fact, is the second root cause of the free-trade paradox. Modernity has emancipated everyone from the limits of location and community. By and large, when we trade, we trade with strangers; when we vote, we vote for strangers; when we watch, read, or listen to stories, the tellers of the tales are strangers. As opposed to the ancestors Tocqueville compares us to, we do not know the people with whom we have to do, in either the economic or the political sphere. This is simply the shadow side of the miracle of markets, which, for the first time in history, have allowed strangers to look after each other. They’ve also allowed each of us to live more and more of our lives exclusively as strangers to other people. This is how Tocqueville — rather pessimistically — describes us: Each, standing apart, is like a stranger to the destiny of others; his children and personal friends forming for him the entire human race. As for the remainder of his fellow citizens, he is beside them, but he does not see them. He touches them, but he does not feel them. He exists only in and for himself.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 事实上，匿名是自由贸易悖论的第二个根本原因。现代性将每个人从地点和社区的限制中解放出来。总的来说，当我们进行交易时，我们是在与陌生人进行交易；当我们投票时，我们投票给陌生人；当我们看、读或听故事时，故事的讲述者都是陌生人。与托克维尔将我们比作的祖先相反，我们不了解我们必须与之打交道的人，无论是在经济领域还是在政治领域。这只是市场奇迹的阴暗面，历史上第一次让陌生人能够互相照顾。它们还让我们每个人越来越多地以陌生人的身份过着自己的生活。托克维尔（相当悲观地）是这样描述我们的：每个人，孤立无援，对他人的命运都像陌生人；每个人都对他人的命运感到陌生。他的孩子和私人朋友为他构成了整个人类。至于其余的同胞，他就在他们旁边，但他看不到他们。他触摸它们，但感觉不到它们。他只存在于他自己之中并为他自己而存在。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) The last sentence but one is as apt a summary as one could hope to come by of how each of us functions in the modern economy: “He touches them, but he does not feel them.”
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 最后一句话是对我们每个人在现代经济中如何运作的最贴切的总结：“他触摸了它们，但他感觉不到它们。”

paragraphs.sourceText: L) This is the greatest challenge facing defenders of free trade. It’s exceedingly difficult for human beings to feel gratitude toward strangers, and the global marketplace that has made us so rich has also made us strangers to one another. Our brains are hardwired for tribal life, and tribes do not take kindly to strangers. Impressing a sense of dependence upon and gratitude toward foreign strangers is therefore an uphill task.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 这是自由贸易捍卫者面临的最大挑战。人类很难对陌生人心怀感激，而全球市场让我们变得如此富有，也让我们彼此变得陌生。我们的大脑天生适合部落生活，而部落不会善待陌生人。因此，让外国人对陌生人产生依赖感和感激之情是一项艰巨的任务。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) If free-traders are going to win policy arguments in the future, they’ll have to find a way of forging bonds of affection between American consumers and foreign producers. Only by de-anonymizing the men and women who supply us with the goods and services we enjoy from overseas and by creating a sense of solidarity and relationship across borders that transcends economic interest can free trade win the day. Otherwise, the inborn biological upper hand that protectionists have in the form of nationalist solidarity is bound to win the day at the ballot box.
paragraphs.translationZh: M）如果自由贸易者想要在未来赢得政策争论，他们就必须找到一种在美国消费者和外国生产商之间建立感情纽带的方法。只有消除向我们提供海外商品和服务的人们的匿名性，并建立超越经济利益的跨国界团结和关系，自由贸易才能赢得胜利。否则，保护主义者以民族主义团结的形式所拥有的先天生物学优势必然会在投票箱中获胜。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. People became more and more reliant on others for basic needs as they entered the modern world even though they might feel less so.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 当人们进入现代世界时，他们在基本需求方面变得越来越依赖他人，尽管他们可能感觉不那么依赖。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. On the topic of trade, productive debates might be possible, in contrast to the familiar mutual condemnation in discussing other issues.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 与讨论其他问题时常见的相互谴责不同，在贸易专题上，可能会进行富有成效的辩论。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. We feel greater independence than we actually possess because money allows us to buy things without building any relationships.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 我们感到比实际拥有的更独立，因为金钱让我们可以在不建立任何关系的情况下购买东西。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. The trouble with today’s trade stems from misconceptions rather than money.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 当今贸易的问题源于误解而不是金钱。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. For their arguments to prevail, advocates of free trade must try to forge bonds of affection between consumers at home and producers overseas.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 为了使他们的论点占上风，自由贸易的倡导者必须努力在国内消费者和海外生产者之间建立感情纽带。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. According to Tocqueville, unlike our ancestors, we and the people we do trade with are strangers to each other.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 根据托克维尔的说法，与我们的祖先不同，我们和与我们进行贸易的人彼此是陌生人。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. In primitive societies, people had to rely mostly on themselves to meet their personal needs.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 在原始社会，人们不得不主要依靠自己来满足个人需要。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Few commodities in American homes are not reliant on people abroad in the process of manufacture and sale.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 美国国内的商品几乎没有在制造和销售过程中不依赖国外的人。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Protectionists argue against free trade by referring to the losses suffered by domestic producers and communities.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 保护主义者以国内生产者和社区遭受的损失为由反对自由贸易。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. It is extremely hard to make people feel dependent on and grateful to strangers overseas.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 要让海外的陌生人产生依赖和感激之情是极其困难的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有 2 段。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A)、B)、C) 和 D)。您应该决定最佳选择，并在答题卡 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: There are hundreds of personality quizzes online that assert they can ascertain whether the right or left half of your brain is dominant. Left-brained people are supposedly logical and excel at language and math while right-brained people are more imaginative, emotionally intelligent and skilled with spatial reasoning. There’s just one problem: That’s not how brains work.
paragraphs.translationZh: 网上有数百个性格测验，声称它们可以确定你的右半脑或左半脑占主导地位。左脑型的人被认为逻辑性强，擅长语言和数学，而右脑型的人则更具想象力、情商和空间推理能力。只有一个问题：大脑不是这样工作的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Popular science enthusiasts sort of took this idea and ran with it, and it’s become woven in popular culture now, and it’s not going away.
paragraphs.translationZh: 科普爱好者们接受了这个想法并付诸实践，它现在已经融入流行文化中，而且不会消失。

paragraphs.sourceText: Despite this enduring belief, there’s no such thing as being “right-brained” or “left-brained”. Whether you’re someone who tends more towards creativity or logic has nothing to do with one hemisphere of your brain being dominant over the other. But the actual science of how the two halves of our brains work together is sometimes stranger than fiction.
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管有这种持久的信念，但并不存在“右脑”或“左脑”之类的东西。无论你是更倾向于创造力还是逻辑性，都与大脑的一个半球是否优于另一个半球无关。但关于我们大脑的两半部分如何协同工作的实际科学有时比小说更奇怪。

paragraphs.sourceText: The human brain is divided into two hemispheres, the left and right. In all vertebrate (脊椎的) animals，the right hemisphere controls the left side of the body and vice versa. And scientists have long known, thanks to the behaviors of patients who suffered brain injuries, that different areas of the brain do different things.
paragraphs.translationZh: 人的大脑分为两个半球，左脑和右脑。在所有脊椎动物中，右半球控制身体的左侧，反之亦然。科学家们早就知道，由于脑损伤患者的行为，大脑的不同区域会做不同的事情。

paragraphs.sourceText: But many scientists struggled with this idea, because the very suggestion that the left and right halves of the brain operate differently disrupted the idea that nature tends toward perfect symmetry.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但许多科学家对这个想法感到困惑，因为左右半脑运作方式不同的建议破坏了自然趋于完美对称的观点。

paragraphs.sourceText: Work by neuroscientists (神经科学家) has revealed the importance of different hemispheres of the brain for different activities. However, their research quickly saw some misinterpretations in the general public: Some presumed creative people must be right-brained and logical people left-brained. It is proven that not only is personality unrelated to the different halves of the brain, but people aren’t really right- or left-brained to begin with. The idea that we have left-dominant people and right-dominant people, and that this is related to personality, is categorically false. That’s never been supported in the neuroscience community. Neuroscientists don’t believe that and never have.
paragraphs.translationZh: 神经科学家（神经科学家）的工作揭示了大脑不同半球对于不同活动的重要性。然而，他们的研究很快就引起了公众的一些误解：一些人认为富有创造力的人必须是右脑型的，而逻辑型的人必须是左脑型的。事实证明，人格不仅与大脑的不同半球无关，而且人们一开始就不是真正的右脑或左脑。认为我们有左主导的人和右主导的人，并且这与性格有关的想法是绝对错误的。这在神经科学界从未得到支持。神经科学家不相信这一点，也从来没有相信过。

paragraphs.sourceText: What scientists learned is that there are really important differences between the left hemisphere and the right hemisphere. It’s just that they have nothing to do with personality or whether cognitive strategy is more logical or free spirited or creative. While researchers have shown the limitations of how the hemispheres of our brains influence our lives, it’s not difficult to understand the appeal of such ideas. People are endlessly fascinated by themselves and their friends, and the subtle differences in how people think about the world are really meaningful to them. When you come up with an online quiz that tells us something about ourselves, we’re drawn to that. It’s irresistible. But you have to take it with an enormous grain of salt.
paragraphs.translationZh: 科学家们了解到，左半球和右半球之间确实存在重要差异。只是它们与个性无关，也与认知策略是否更具逻辑性、自由精神或创造性无关。虽然研究人员已经证明了大脑半球影响我们生活的局限性，但不难理解这些想法的吸引力。人们对自己和朋友有着无尽的着迷，人们看待世界的细微差别对他们来说确实很有意义。当你想出一个在线测验来告诉我们一些关于我们自己的事情时，我们就会被它吸引。这是不可抗拒的。但你必须对此持保留态度。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: One hundred thirty-five students, four teachers, one giant classroom: This is what 9th grade looks like at Westwood High School, in Mesa, Arizona’s largest school system. There, an innovative teaching model has taken hold, and is spreading to other schools in the district and beyond.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一百三十五名学生、四名教师、一间巨大的教室：这就是韦斯特伍德高中九年级的样子，该高中位于亚利桑那州最大的学校系统梅萨。在那里，一种创新的教学模式已经形成，并正在推广到该地区及其他地区的其他学校。

paragraphs.sourceText: Five years ago, faced with high teacher turnover and declining student enrollment, Westwood’s leaders decided to try something different. Working with professors at Arizona State University’s teachers college, they piloted a classroom model known as team teaching, which allows teachers to dissolve the walls that separate their classes across physical or grade divides.
paragraphs.translationZh: 五年前，面对教师流动率高和学生入学率下降的情况，韦斯特伍德的领导者决定尝试一些不同的东西。他们与亚利桑那州立大学师范学院的教授合作，试行了一种称为团队教学的课堂模式，该模式允许教师消除物理或年级分隔班级的墙壁。

paragraphs.sourceText: The teachers share large groups of students — sometimes 100 or more — and rotate between group instruction, one-on-one interventions, small study groups, or whatever the teachers as a team agree is a priority that day. What looks at times like chaos is in fact a carefully orchestrated plan: Each morning, the Westwood teams meet to hammer out a personalized program for every student the team will focus on that day.
paragraphs.translationZh: 教师们与一大群学生（有时 100 名或更多）一起轮流进行小组教学、一对一干预、小型学习小组或教师团队一致同意的当天优先事项。有时看似混乱的事情实际上是一个精心策划的计划：每天早上，Westwood 团队都会开会，为团队当天要关注的每个学生制定个性化计划。

paragraphs.sourceText: By giving teachers more opportunity to collaborate, Mesa’s administrators hoped to fill staffing gaps and boost teacher morale and retention. Initial research suggests the gamble could pay off.
paragraphs.translationZh: 梅萨的管理人员希望通过为教师提供更多合作机会来填补人员缺口，提高教师士气和保留率。初步研究表明，这场赌博可能会得到回报。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Teachers are doing fantastic things, but it’s very rare a teacher walks into another room to see what’s happening,” said Andi Fourlis, superintendent of Mesa Public Schools. “Our profession is so slow to advance because we are working in isolation.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 梅萨公立学校的校长安迪·福利斯 (Andi Fourlis) 表示：“老师们正在做着很棒的事情，但很少有老师走进另一个房间来看看发生了什么。” “我们的职业发展如此缓慢，因为我们是孤立工作的。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Of course, overhauling teaching approaches can’t fix all the frustrations teachers have, such as low pay, but early results from Mesa show team teaching may be helping to reverse low morale. In a survey of hundreds of the district’s teachers, researchers found those who worked on teams reported greater job satisfaction, more frequent collaborations with colleagues, and more positive interactions with students.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当然，彻底改革教学方法并不能解决教师面临的所有挫折，例如工资低，但梅萨的早期结果显示，团队教学可能有助于扭转低落的士气。在对该学区数百名教师的调查中，研究人员发现，那些以团队形式工作的教师的工作满意度更高，与同事的合作更频繁，与学生的互动也更积极。

paragraphs.sourceText: Another benefit of teams, teachers say, is that they can help each other improve their instruction. During one planning session, English teacher Jeff Hall shared a performance appraisal with a science teacher: Her recent lecture on something she called “the central dogma of biology” had bewildered him and their other teammates.
paragraphs.translationZh: 老师们说，团队的另一个好处是他们可以互相帮助改进教学。在一次计划会议上，英语老师杰夫·霍尔与一位科学老师分享了一次绩效评估：她最近关于她所谓的“生物学中心教条”的讲座让他和其他队友感到困惑。

paragraphs.sourceText: “If the science is too confusing for me, can you imagine the frustration you feel as kids?” Hall said. But the science teacher, he said, wouldn’t have known about the confusion on her own.
paragraphs.translationZh: “如果科学对我来说太令人困惑，你能想象你小时候感受到的挫败感吗？”霍尔说。但他说，科学老师自己不会知道这种混乱。

paragraphs.sourceText: The model is not for everyone. Some teachers approached about volunteering for a team have said they prefer to work alone. Team teaching can also be a scheduling nightmare, especially at schools like Westwood where only some staff work in teams. There are also thorny questions like how to evaluate four teachers on the performance of 135 students. But for the time being, it seems to be working.
paragraphs.translationZh: 该模型并不适合所有人。一些寻求加入团队志愿者的老师表示，他们更喜欢单独工作。团队教学也可能是日程安排的噩梦，尤其是在像 Westwood 这样的学校，那里只有一些教职员工以团队形式工作。还有一些棘手的问题，比如如何根据 135 名学生的表现来评估 4 名老师。但就目前而言，它似乎正在发挥作用。
